entries.title: a shutdown checkpoints a database without migrating it
entries.summary: At shutdown the server compacts the WAL of every database in its storage directory. It opened each one through the indexer's connection, which creates the index schema or runs the version migrations. A database still being created raised no such table out of the shutdown, any other SQLite file there (telemetry.db) gained the index tables, and a file that is not a database stopped the loop. The checkpoint now opens a plain connection and never raises. Index tables an earlier shutdown created in another database stay there.

entries.title: a fusion search scores no query against another model's vectors
entries.summary: After a change of embedding model, search_symbols with fusion=true embedded the query with the new model and scored it against the old model's stored vectors, reporting the semantic channel as ok. It now compares what built the stored vectors before it calls the provider. On a mismatch it scores no similarity, fuses the other channels and returns semantic_store_mismatch with the reason; run embed_repo to rebuild. One store changes on upgrade: vectors with no metadata are not scored by a fusion search until embed_repo runs.

entries.title: a read-only open reads the file the path names
entries.summary: Where the storage directory's name held #, a percent escape or ?, every read-only reader opened another file: under a directory named c#proj the open was writable on a stray empty file c, and the embedding store reported no vectors over a store that held them. The path is now escaped where the SQLite URI is built, so those readers see what is stored. A path without those characters opens as before.

entries.title: a semantic search writes no vector of a second model
entries.summary: After a change of embedding model, one semantic search_symbols on a repo with a new symbol wrote that symbol's vector at the new width beside the old ones; the mixed store then scored nothing semantically and called the provider again on every search. The search now compares what built the stored vectors before it writes. On a mismatch it writes nothing, ranks without the semantic channel and returns semantic_store_mismatch with the reason; run embed_repo to rebuild. One store changes on upgrade: vectors with no metadata (left by a full re-index before 1.108.331) are no longer scored until embed_repo runs.
